input.query: What must the gateway do after excessive clock drift, including recovery when the reference clock is unavailable?

state.output:

Result 1: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vanilla1999/DocAtlas/e62fa9e357bd22731cddabe930532a4a2faecc18/eval/blind_project_context/step14-host-language-live/frozen-corpus/architecture

# Scheduler architecture
Meridian separates ownership, planning, execution and display to permit independent restarts.
## Planner
The planner solves interval conflicts using instrument availability and reservation priority. It can compute a plan while execution is suspended. A computed plan is not permission to bypass a weather interlock or clock check.
## Prototype recovery
The retired prototype cleared pending reservations when time drifted and restarted on its first local clock sample. These behaviours must not be used to recover the current gateway.

------------------------------------------------------------
Result 2: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vanilla1999/DocAtlas/e62fa9e357bd22731cddabe930532a4a2faecc18/eval/blind_project_context/step14-host-language-live/frozen-corpus/clock

# Time coordination
The gateway compares instrument time with the observatory reference before executing a schedule.
## Clock offset
If the absolute clock offset exceeds two seconds, pause schedule execution and notify the duty operator. Keep queued reservations unchanged. Resume only after two consecutive reference checks report an offset within two seconds.
## Missing reference
If the reference clock is unavailable, keep execution paused; a local clock reading alone cannot satisfy either recovery check.

------------------------------------------------------------
Result 3: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vanilla1999/DocAtlas/e62fa9e357bd22731cddabe930532a4a2faecc18/eval/blind_project_context/step14-host-language-live/frozen-corpus/weather

# Weather decisions
Weather decisions govern execution, not ownership of reservations.
## Suspension
Suspend outdoor observations when the wind interlock opens. Preserve reservation identifiers during suspension. Resume only after the interlock closes and the duty operator records a restart approval.
## Indoor instrument
An instrument explicitly classified as indoor may continue during a wind suspension, provided its own safety interlocks remain closed. A roof visible as closed on the calendar does not establish indoor classification.

------------------------------------------------------------
Result 4: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vanilla1999/DocAtlas/e62fa9e357bd22731cddabe930532a4a2faecc18/eval/blind_project_context/step14-host-language-live/frozen-corpus/reservations

# Confirmed reservations
These rules apply to confirmed night-time reservations on shared instruments.
For orientation, the reservation console links to the calendar's [colour legend](calendar.md#colours).
## Transfer
Transfer a reservation only after the receiving observer accepts it and the duty operator approves the transfer. Retain the original reservation identifier and record both observers in the audit trail. A transfer does not alter the [weather suspension](weather.md#suspension).
## Locked instrument
If the instrument has an active maintenance lock, leave the transfer pending even after observer acceptance and operator approval. The lock must be cleared by the instrument team first.

------------------------------------------------------------
Result 5: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vanilla1999/DocAtlas/e62fa9e357bd22731cddabe930532a4a2faecc18/eval/blind_project_context/step14-host-language-live/frozen-corpus/clock

## Simulation clock
The simulator advances time manually and never waits for reference checks. Its accelerated clock is isolated from the real instrument gateway.

part.text:
If the absolute clock offset **exceeds two seconds**, the gateway must:

- Pause schedule execution and notify the duty operator.
- Keep queued reservations unchanged.
- Resume only after **two consecutive checks against the observatory reference clock** each report an offset within two seconds.

If the reference clock is unavailable, execution must remain paused. A local clock reading alone cannot satisfy either recovery check. [Time coordination: Clock offset and Missing reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vanilla1999/DocAtlas/e62fa9e357bd22731cddabe930532a4a2faecc18/eval/blind_project_context/step14-host-language-live/frozen-corpus/clock.md)

The retired prototype’s recovery behavior—clearing pending reservations and restarting on the first local clock sample—must not be used for the current gateway. The planner may compute a plan while execution is suspended, but that plan does not bypass the clock check or a weather interlock. [Scheduler architecture: Planner and Prototype recovery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vanilla1999/DocAtlas/e62fa9e357bd22731cddabe930532a4a2faecc18/eval/blind_project_context/step14-host-language-live/frozen-corpus/architecture.md)
